test: test_run_firstFaultWinsPriority

why: parking the drive still counts as the motor loop answering, so a parked machine stays free of a communication fault

test: test_dev_servo_setPositionClearsArrival
given: a motor drive parked on a target, then given a new origin at the current encoder, then one control tick
then: redefining the encoder origin clears the previous arrival immediately, then the next tick reports arrival at that origin
why: homing moves the target with the origin, so arrival is judged again in the new frame

test: test_dev_servo_setPositionUpdatesEncoderAndTarget
given: a motor drive whose origin is set to a new encoder count
then: setting the motor drive origin writes that count to the encoder and to the target

test: test_dev_servo_setVelocityClearsArrival
given: a motor drive parked on a position target, then commanded to a non-zero speed
then: a speed command issued after arrival clears that arrival immediately
why: the motion controller retires a move on arrival, so leaving a position target drops that arrival at once

test: test_dev_servo_velocityModeCommandsPulseTrain
given: an enabled motor drive commanded to hold a non-zero speed
then: a speed command starts a pulse train and the motor drive reports a non-zero commanded speed

test: test_dev_servo_stallWhenCommandedWithoutMotion
given: an enabled motor drive commanded at high speed while the encoder stays frozen for longer than the stall window
then: commanding motion while the encoder stays still is reported as a stall
why: a jammed carriage is reported as a stall so the controller can stop pulling against the jam

test: test_dev_servo_initialStateDisabledAtTarget
given: a motor drive just after start-up
then: a freshly started motor drive is disabled, arrived at the encoder position, with zero speed and no stall

test: test_dev_servo_stopClearsArrival
given: a motor drive parked on a position target, then stopped
then: a stop issued after arrival clears that arrival immediately
why: the motion controller retires a move on arrival, so a stop drops that arrival at once

test: test_dev_servo_stopRequestsZeroVelocityTarget
given: an enabled motor drive holding a non-zero speed, then a stop, with the encoder free to follow
then: a stop requests a speed of zero, and commanded speed winds down to rest once the encoder tracks the commanded position
why: stopping is a speed hold at rest, so the carriage decelerates under the same accel limit as any other speed change

test: test_dev_stepper_disableDuringMoveStopsTrain
given: a stepper in the middle of a move, then disabled
then: disabling the stepper during a move stops the pulse train and leaves the stepper disabled

test: test_dev_stepper_disableFromStoppedReturnsToDisabled
given: an enabled stepper sitting stopped, then disabled
then: disabling a stopped stepper returns the stepper to disabled on the next cycle

test: test_dev_stepper_enableEntersStopped
given: a disabled stepper that is enabled, then one control cycle
then: enabling the stepper takes effect on the next cycle, leaving the stepper stopped with the pulse train idle

test: test_dev_stepper_moveCompletesToStopped
given: a stepper whose pulse train then reports the move finished
then: when the pulse train finishes, the stepper reports the target position, then on the next cycle stops the train and reports arrival

test: test_dev_stepper_moveNegativeIsCCW
given: an enabled stepper commanded from zero to a lower position
then: a move to a lower position starts a counter-clockwise pulse train of the remaining steps at the commanded rate

test: test_dev_stepper_movePositiveIsCW
given: an enabled stepper commanded from zero to a higher position
then: a move to a higher position starts a clockwise pulse train of the remaining steps at the commanded rate

test: test_dev_stepper_moveRejectsZeroSpeed
given: a move commanded at zero steps per second
then: a move at zero steps per second is refused and leaves the target unchanged

test: test_dev_stepper_moveFromNonZeroStart
given: an enabled stepper sitting at a non-zero origin, commanded to a higher position
then: a move from a non-zero start starts a pulse train whose length is the distance from the current position to the target

test: test_dev_stepper_moveStagesTarget
given: a stepper commanded to a new position at a non-zero rate
then: a move records the new target immediately and reports the stepper as still moving

test: test_dev_stepper_movingAccumulatesStepsCW
given: a stepper moving clockwise, with the pulse train reporting pulses emitted so far
then: while the stepper is moving clockwise, reported steps equal the start position plus the pulses emitted so far

test: test_dev_stepper_movingAccumulatesStepsCCW
given: a stepper moving counter-clockwise, with the pulse train reporting pulses emitted so far
then: while the stepper is moving counter-clockwise, reported steps equal the start position minus the pulses emitted so far

test: test_dev_stepper_isReadyStagedByRun
given: a stepper just after start-up, then after one control cycle
then: a stepper reports unready until the first control cycle, and ready from then on even while disabled
why: the controller treats an answering stepper as the motor loop running, and a silent stepper as a communication fault

test: test_dev_stepper_setPositionAppliedOnRun
given: a stepper whose origin is set to a new count, then one control cycle
then: a new origin is applied to reported steps on the next cycle

test: test_dev_stepper_initialStateDisabled
given: a stepper just after start-up
then: a freshly started stepper is disabled, at rest at position zero, and reports arrival

test: test_dev_stepper_stopRequestEndsMove
given: a stepper in the middle of a move, then stopped
then: a stop ends the move on the next cycle, stopping the pulse train and leaving the stepper at rest

test: test_dev_stepper_stoppedAtTargetStaysStopped
given: an enabled stepper whose target is already the current position
then: an enabled stepper already on its target stays stopped with the pulse train idle

test: test_dev_stepper_velocityModeIntegratesAndReverses
given: an enabled stepper commanded to a speed, then reversed, then stopped
then: in speed mode the stepper integrates emitted pulses into position, a reverse restarts the pulse train so position stays continuous, and a stop halts the train
why: a reverse restarts the pulse train from the current position so the reported position stays continuous through the turn

test: test_dev_stepper_zeroPositionResetsSteps
given: a stepper sitting at a non-zero origin, then zeroed
then: zeroing the stepper origin sets reported steps to zero on the next cycle

test: test_app_testManagement_manualMoveSlotsBounded
given: five jogs issued before any has run
then: four jogs can wait to run; a fifth is refused, and the four waiting jogs run on the next cycle
why: jogs wait one cycle to run, so only a handful can be waiting

test: test_app_testManagement_happyPathLifecycle
given: a test started, the program finished, then the crosshead idle
then: a test runs until the program is finished and the crosshead is idle, then reports that the test is complete and becomes idle
why: the crosshead has to finish the last move before the test is called complete

test: test_app_testManagement_g122TerminatesFeed
given: a running test whose program has a linear move followed by G122
then: G122 marks the end of the program, so only the linear move is run, and once the crosshead is idle the test is reported complete
why: G122 is the end-of-program mark the firmware waits on before calling the test complete

test: test_app_testManagement_manualMoveGatedWhileBusy
given: a jog while idle, then a start, then another jog
then: a jog is accepted while idle, and refused once a test start is waiting to begin
why: a jog must not be mixed into a test that is about to run

test: test_app_testManagement_openFailureEndsStart
given: a start whose motion program cannot be opened
then: a start whose motion program cannot be opened reports an error, aborts, and leaves the machine idle
why: a missing program must not leave the machine looking as if a test is running

test: test_app_testManagement_motionDisabledAbortsRun
given: a running test, then motion turned off
then: motion turning off mid-test aborts the remaining moves and warns that the test was aborted
why: the operator needs to know the test stopped because motion was turned off

test: test_app_testManagement_userEndStopsRun
given: a running test, then the operator stopping it
then: an operator stop aborts the remaining moves and leaves the machine idle, with no toast
why: the operator already knows they stopped the test

test: test_m5_restart_reaches_running_after_each_terminal
given: after an operator stop, a motion-off abort, a sample-limit stop, and a failed open, in turn
then: after every way a test can finish, a new start reaches a running test
why: a finished session has to fully return to idle, or the next test would never start

test: test_app_testManagement_sampleLimitAbortsRun
given: a running test, then the sample past its force limit
then: the sample going past its own limit mid-test aborts the remaining moves and warns that the test was stopped
why: the specimen's configured limit is what stops the test

test: test_app_testManagement_doubleStartRejected
given: a start already accepted, then a second start before that test has finished
then: a second start is refused while the first is still waiting to begin, and refused again once that test is running
why: two tests must never run at once; a start already accepted already counts as a session under way

test: test_m5_lifecycle_start_manual_matrix
given: idle, a start waiting to begin, a running test, and after every way a test can finish
then: a new start and a jog are accepted while idle, including after every way a test can finish, and refused while a start is waiting to begin or a test is running

test: test_app_testManagement_startNotDroppedWhenMotionLags
given: a start accepted while motion is still off for one cycle, then motion coming on
then: a start accepted while motion is still off stays waiting through that cycle, and the test begins once motion is on
why: motion enable is applied one cycle later than the start request, so the start has to wait

test: test_lib_timer_expiredIsSticky
given: an expired one-shot timer whose clock then appears to go backwards
then: an expired one-shot timer stays expired even if the clock appears to go backwards
why: a fired timeout is a latch; a clock glitch must not un-fire it

test: test_lib_timer_expires_across_uint32_ms_wrap
given: a 100 millisecond one-shot timer started 20 milliseconds before the millisecond clock wraps, then checked 51 and 111 milliseconds later
then: a one-shot timer started just before the millisecond clock wraps expires only after a full period of modular elapsed time
why: the millisecond clock wraps after about 49 days; unsigned wrap-around is how elapsed time is measured

test: test_lib_timer_expiresStrictlyAfterPeriod
given: a 100 millisecond one-shot timer checked at exactly 100 milliseconds and again at 101
then: a one-shot timer checked at exactly its period is still running, and has expired one millisecond later
why: expiry uses a strict greater-than so a timer never fires early

test: test_lib_timer_initIsOff
given: a newly created one-shot timer with a 100 millisecond period
then: a newly created one-shot timer is off and has not expired

test: test_lib_timer_near_zero_start_no_spurious_expiry
given: a 100 millisecond one-shot timer started at time zero and checked at 50 milliseconds, then at 101
then: a one-shot timer started at time zero has not expired at 50 milliseconds, and has expired one millisecond past its period
why: subtracting the period from a smaller now would wrap and look expired immediately after start

test: test_lib_timer_restartReArms
given: an expired one-shot timer that is started again from a later clock
then: starting an expired one-shot timer re-arms that timer from now, so expiry waits a full period from the new start

test: test_lib_timer_startRuns
given: an off one-shot timer that is started
then: a started one-shot timer is running

test: test_lib_timer_stopReturnsToOff
given: a running one-shot timer that is stopped, then left well past its period
then: a stopped one-shot timer is off and does not expire, even after its period has passed

test: test_watchdog
given: every supervised loop starts checking in, then three seconds pass with no check-in, then only the monitor loop checks in, then every loop checks in
then: supervised loops that go three seconds without a check-in are all reported dead; a check-in from the monitor loop revives only that loop; a check-in from every loop reports them all alive
why: a wedged loop still counts as a running core, so the check-in is what catches a stall before the machine keeps moving unsupervised

test: first_position_becomes_the_baseline
given: the very first position report, whatever its absolute value
then: the first position report becomes the zero of extension
why: the machine does not home to 0, so absolute position is not extension

test: engagement_slack_is_consumed_before_extension
given: travel smaller than the configured engagement slack
then: extension stays at zero until travel exceeds the engagement slack
why: the sample is not yet loaded, so reporting strain would be wrong

test: tension_direction_is_configurable
given: a machine whose tensile travel decreases machine position
then: on a machine whose tensile direction is decreasing position, moving to a smaller position produces positive extension
why: the DS2 gantry and the EdgeBoard gantry pull in opposite senses
